Calorie Calculator

Estimate daily calorie maintenance from a resting-energy equation and an activity multiplier, then model a modest goal adjustment. This gives a planning starting point, not a measured metabolic rate or a prescribed diet. The calculator applies Mifflin–St Jeor resting energy expenditure and multiplies by the selected activity factor. The goal adjustment is user-entered and is shown separately from estimated maintenance.

How to use this calculator

  1. Enter weight, height, age and the remaining inputs.
  2. Select Calculate to see the answer and its breakdown.
  3. Keep a scenario, change an input and compare the results.

Use consistent units and check the assumptions below before applying the result.

How calorie is calculated

The calculator applies Mifflin–St Jeor resting energy expenditure and multiplies by the selected activity factor. The goal adjustment is user-entered and is shown separately from estimated maintenance. A 35-year-old, 70 kg, 170 cm woman estimates about 1,420 kcal/day at rest; a light-activity factor of 1.375 gives roughly 1,953 kcal/day maintenance.

Daily estimate=Mifflin–St Jeor resting energy×activity multiplier+entered adjustment.
A worked example

A 35-year-old, 70 kg, 170 cm woman estimates about 1,420 kcal/day at rest; a light-activity factor of 1.375 gives roughly 1,953 kcal/day maintenance.

Assumptions & useful context

Not medical nutrition advice; large or medically restricted targets need professional guidance.

Health calculations are estimates for education. They cannot diagnose a condition or replace a clinician’s assessment. Individual needs vary, especially during pregnancy, illness and growth.

Mifflin–St Jeor equation paper (PubMed) ↗

Frequently asked questions

Is the result my exact calorie need?

No. It is an equation-based estimate and can differ from measured needs.

Does the goal adjustment guarantee weight change?

No. Real intake, activity, health, and metabolic adaptation affect outcomes.
